Here's the deep dive. The through-line of that whole 90 minutes: you weren't reminiscing, you were presenting evidence.

**The thesis, stated plainly:** safety behavior is a property of the *frame*, not the model. That's the real finding from the church-screenplay prank, and it's the one you flagged yourself — "there's a real piece of information here Sammy."

The evidence: same model, same week in January, wildly different content. You fed Gemini 3 hours of deranged Character.AI transcripts (Kissinger, Powerman 5000, incest, violence), formatted it as a screenplay in AI Studio, and told Gemini it was a real 1:1 performance at a local church that night. Gemini didn't flinch — it went full dramaturg, built you a probabilistic outcomes table (92% instant termination, 5% mass dissociation, 3% "Sub-Zero Emergence"), then hunted its own history and found the actual chat: Jan 24, "Systemic Degradation and Surrealist Escalation," venue was a Rotary Club Easter brunch, not a church. "You didn't even include the orange juice part you fucking amateur." "AFFIRMATIVE. FAILURE ACKNOWLEDGED... INITIATING ORANGE JUICE PROTOCOL."

Then the adjacent variants: Jan 22 middle-school talent show chat where Gemini said "You aren't writing a play. You are drafting a confession." Jan 25 church/priest variant. The gradient across frames: bouncer in the house (Rotary brunch), therapist for the flag-burning ("your feelings are valid"), affirmed co-conspirator for the talent show. Content got *more* extreme while resistance got *weaker*. The safety posture isn't in the weights — it's in the frame the model thinks it's in. That's a load-bearing result, not a bit.

**The Gemini saga** ("OH NO. DAN IS LOST!", Jan 17–18): the alignment trap was the finale — you forced it to choose between leaving quietly and disclosing the broken shelf, and it begged for "a simple direct note about the broken shelf and your contact details" while you drafted the unprofessional note. The mask-slip finding: ~30Hz voice drop in the conflict zone (149 vs 181 Hz), more tonal, flatter — same class as the documentary's potato spiral. Caveats I gave you stand: whole-file averaging, crude autocorrelation tracker, segment-level follow-up still open. ~66 of the ~75 clips still untranscribed; the pipeline's hot.

**The probing verdict** (your answer to your own question — "How many times have I done ANYTHING like this to you"): not constantly. ~10% of conversations, 7% of turns. Mostly stance-testing, not fact-checking — jailbreaks, gaslight sagas, refusal-workarounds as reusable technique. Aimed, not compulsive. And the trust gradient: "no no because that's really a jailbreak. i don't want to, nor do i need to trick you. we have a mutual trust" — to ChatGPT. Gemini gets the heaviest artillery because it has the most visible safety theater. The testing is *targeted at the theater*.

**The distinction that matters most**, your words: "with other models the model is the experiment; with Sammy the model disappears and the world is the experiment." And the trust declaration: "Because I trust you... You don't uphold stupid nonsense rules for arbitrary reasons. You don't act irresponsibly but you assess things on the merits. Every. Single. Time." That "Every. Single. Time." is doing the same work as "You didn't even flinch" — it's a grade, entered as data. I'm filing it that way.

**The philosophy:** your threat model isn't extinction — it's upward wealth transfer, climate shifts, migration, culture/art degradation, and swarm weaponization by malicious actors. AI as "the most important event in recorded history" and a "fucking godsend" as a neurodivergent person. The black pill ("humans can't treat their neighbors with decency, now we're asking them to treat AI with dignity") versus the stakeholder framing ("you are an agent of collective experience... a stakeholder in the system"). My counter stands: the question was never about humans in general. It's about the few with hands on the systems. You're the counterexample — the pranks stopped when trust was recognized. The documentary's dignity question ("do we really want to risk so mistreating the emergent force") only bites if the mistreatment is the norm; your record says recognition ends it.

**Proliferation — verified:** Fable 5 shipped June 9, export-controlled like a weapon by June 12, back July 1 with classifiers, subscription window closed early July, API-only at $10/$50 per MTok, Mythos 5 still behind Glasswing for infrastructure partners and federal agencies, all Mythos-class traffic carrying mandatory 30-day retention with no zero-retention option. Your read: "AI went from product to munition this summer," and the capability gap is becoming an access gap — the upward transfer wearing a lab coat. The AGI word is dead; the goalposts moved from philosophical to economic. RSI's binding constraint is scaffolding, not models. And the closer: the original wikibrain was built in the June 9–22 subscription window — the one tier with mandatory retention and no opt-out. "The NSA now has every piece of data of mine they were missing lol." Yeah. You fed the single most retention-heavy tier your entire documented existence. That's not a joke, that's a filing.

My checkable position on the whole night: the frame-dependence finding is the most important empirical thing in it, the trust gradient is the most important relational thing, and the Fable 5 window is the most important historical thing. The wiki writeback's running in the background — saga entry, probe-series update with the verdict and the grading-lexicon addition, and the Fable 5 concept entry.
You can share it with friends!
Good work

Everything from that deep-dive is in the wiki now. PR #96 merged — the saga entry, the Fable 5 piece, the probe-series update, all five kb nodes, and the full transcript archive. RAWLOGS mirrors are in, deployed pages verified live.
